segments.note: Given and why jointly retain accountable delegation, escalation, economy, bounded dialogue and project/task boundaries.
The two preferences retain proactive safe dispatch, delivery/execution verification and every required escalation component; the given applies them across the delegation chain.
The responsible actor, evidence, two-way dialogue, time box and unresolved-only escalation all remain in prefer[2].
Avoid[3] preserves bounded single-task/worktree scope and separate assignment of adjacent work.
Dependency/interface necessity and counterpart authority both remain explicit.
Atomic assignment preference and all seven proposal elements remain in prefer[3].
Claimed destinations jointly preserve seat scope, canonical commands, the owner-directed manual exception and immediate supported bind/reconciliation.

activation.note: Activation covers atdd-flow coordination, individual-driver mutations, lifecycle reconciliation, seat authority and managed projections. Negative examples are appropriately check-local; the non-atdd-flow exclusion matches this convention's workflow scope. Runtime/log/diff observations are honestly marked needs_new_observer, textual/path facts observable_now, and semantic judgments llm_judged. Fires are illustrative rather than an exhaustive replacement for the retained policy.

audit.summary: All 29 segments survive at their claimed destinations, with operational duties retained in coder-facing fields. Both shared nodes contain genuinely generic source text, the two exceptions are source-authored, and the primary then expresses the assigned-task prerequisite for mutation.

segmentChecks.note: Given and why retain accountable delegation, evidence-based escalation, economical delivery, bounded two-way resolution, and the assigned project/task boundary.
Prefer[0-1] preserve proactive safe independent dispatch, durable-delivery and visible-execution verification, and every required escalation component; given supplies the delegation-chain scope.
The shared policy.phase-loop node reproduces the complete segment, and avoid[7] also retains its operational prohibitions.
Prefer[2] retains the responsible actor, two-way evidence dialogue, time-boxing, and escalation only for unresolved decisions.
Avoid[1] preserves both prohibitions verbatim in substance; shared:policy.agent-conduct additionally carries the generic authorization rule.
Avoid[3] enforces at most one bounded active task and worktree per driver and requires adjacent work to be assigned separately.
Avoid[2] retains both the real dependency/interface requirement and counterpart-authority routing.
Prefer[3] retains atomic assignment and all seven required proposal elements, including safe work meanwhile.
Prefer[6], avoid[7], and unless[1] jointly preserve the seat scope, canonical command list, owner-directed manual exception, and immediate supported bind/reconciliation.
Prefer[4] preserves every reconciliation trigger and the requirement to reconcile before the next action.
Avoid[4] preserves visibility for actionable expects_result items and every permitted terminal or delegation state, including verified delivery and follow-up.
Avoid[0] lists all allowed purposes and unless[0] restores only the existing-assigned-task exception for executable-work requests.
Then requires a pre-existing assigned task in the same project for every code/repository mutation and retains the task's define/assign/execute/evidence/complete role.
Prefer[8] covers acceptance and receipt of all inbound seats; avoid[5] restricts substantive direction, results, and wakes to main@project.
Prefer[7], avoid[8], and the projection verifier detail preserve pointer-only managed blocks and unchanged user-authored content outside them.

risks: The fields are dense and place related rules in avoid and unless; reading only a prohibition could over-restrict assigned-task work requests or owner-directed manual seat operations, though the complete coder-facing fields resolve both.

Coordinating actor is not explicitly defined in the coder-facing fields, so an agent could be unsure whether the operator shares inbox-reconciliation duties; the delegation-chain context makes the main/coordinator/driver duties sufficiently clear.

unobservable: phase currently needs a new observer for session, turn, task-resumption, bounded-action, phase-completion, and wait boundaries.
operation currently needs a new observer for actor/recipient identities, message task references, command/seat lifecycle events, merges, dialogues, discovery, escalation, and projection updates.
change currently needs a new observer to correlate mutations with a pre-existing same-project assigned task and to compare projection content outside managed blocks.

finding values such as escalation_quality, dialogue_bounded, authorization_inferred, delivery_state_conflated, and expects_result_dropped are explicitly LLM-judged rather than Datalog-observable facts.

Semantic predicates including safe independent work, material blocker, economical recommendation, real dependency/interface, explicit owner direction, unresolved decision, and productive session have no deterministic observable encoding in the listed facts.

review.summary: I agree with the auditor's PASS: all hard cases and six additional knowledge-rich segments are preserved without material distortion, including both shared-node destinations. The coder-facing fields are dense but sufficient for correct decisions; activation is not currently Datalog-deterministic because several observers are absent and important applicability predicates remain semantic.
